items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO HIGHER EDUCATION

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4135

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the education law, in relation to allowing dental
residents to satisfy the ethics and jurisprudence educational course
requirement for licensure during the period of their dental residency
and in relation to limited permits in dentistry


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This legislation will remove excess barriers to dental residencies and
permit dental residents to take the mandated dental ethics training
course during the period of their residency

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1 would amend Section 6604-a of Article 133 of the Education
Law to allow dental residents to take the mandatory dental ethics
training course during the period of their residency.

Section 2 would amend Section 6605 of Article 133 of the Education Law
to exempt graduates of dental schools who are in approved residency
programs from having to obtain limited permits.

Section 2 would provide that the law take effect on the one hundred
eightieth day after it shall have become law, provided that Section 1
of the bill would take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Dental school graduates enrolled in approved residencies under the
State Education Department requirements should not be required to
obtain limited permits, which require applications and time-consuming
waits for approval. Medical school graduates are not required to have
limited permits. Once a dental school graduate is enrolled in a
residency approved by the Department, there are sufficient
institutional safeguards to protect the public. with respect to the
mandatory dental ethics training, all other mandatory educational
courses for dentists - infection control training, child abuse
reporting training, cardiopulmonary resuscitation training and tobacco
risks training are able to be satisfied by dental residents during the
period of their residency.  However, due to a flaw in the law, only
ethics training does not permit dental residents to take the required
coursework during their residency period. Since the mandatory ethics
course is one-time training that must be a specific curriculum
approved by the Education Department, it makes the least sense to have
that as the only continuing education requirement that cannot be taken
by dental residents during the period of their residency program. This
bill fixes that problem by allowing dental residents to take that
mandatory course, just like all the other mandatory course
requirements can be taken, during the period of the dental residency.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
